content:
Jessica: Heads-up — kicking off an integration/triage thread for the FlashAttention v2/v3 merge (internal codename: orchid). Found a perf divergence on long contexts in local bench.
Owen: +1 what's the high-level symptom?
Jessica: p95 latency spikes for sequences >8k tokens after switching to v3 kernels in our microbench. FA2 p95 ~220ms -> FA3 p95 ~250ms on same hardware. Also higher KV page faults observed.
Lucas: can you paste the microbench output you ran?
Jessica: ```
# microbench - model=gpt-like seq=8192 batch=1 kernel=flashv3
tokens/sec: 180
p50: 120ms
p95: 250ms
kv-miss-rate: 0.18
# microbench - kernel=flashv2
tokens/sec: 200
p50: 110ms
p95: 220ms
kv-miss-rate: 0.02
```
Priya: kv-miss-rate 0.18 is pretty bad — suggests interaction with paged-KV. Did you run with paged eviction mode=auto?
Jessica: yes, default paged eviction. Hypothesis: v3 changed memory access pattern (larger internal chunks) causing more page churn.
Mike: FA3 may do different blocking / chunk sizes which impacts TLB and page faults. Also could affect continuous-batching coalescing.
Owen: we should isolate batching vs kernel effect. Try disabling continuous-batching and re-run.
Lucas: also test fp16 vs q4/qat quant paths; selection logic might pick different GEMM kernels.
Jessica: Proposed plan: 1) reproduce on a small canary pool, 2) add telemetry for kv-page-faults + per-kernel stall metrics, 3) implement a selector fflag that routes by seq-length + kv_miss heuristics, 4) staged rollout with manual gates.
Priya: what's the fflag schema look like?
Jessica: ```json
{"orchid_attn_selector": {"rules": [
 {"if": "seq<=1024", "kernel":"flashv3"},
 {"if": "seq>1024 and kv_miss_rate<0.05", "kernel":"flashv3"},
 {"else": "flashv2"}
]}}
```
Owen: nice. Add a runtime safety fallback chain: flashv3 -> flashv2 -> fused-attn -> reference-slow so we never block traffic.
Jessica: agreed — fallback order implemented. Also will default to flashv2 if selector throws.
Mike: Monitoring/alerts: create dashboard showing p50/p95 latency, kv_miss_rate, gpu_stall_ms, gpu_util, alloc-failures, error-rate. Alert if p95 > baseline * 1.10 for 15m or kv_miss_rate > 0.08.
Lucas: Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 6h -> 25% for 12h -> 100% after 24h if stable. Manual pause gate at each step.
Priya: don't forget regression checks: run prompt-suite A/B to detect quality regressions (hallucination, tokenization diffs).
Jessica: infra-bot: create canary pool 'orchid-canary-1' with tag=attn-orchid size=6 gpus
infra-bot: ✅ created pool orchid-canary-1 (6 x a100-smoketest)
telemetry-bot: dashboard 'orchid-canary' created, baseline snapshot saved as snapshot_3740001234
Owen: quick smoke commands for ops?
Jessica: `build/kernel:enable --flag=orchid_attn_selector --pool=orchid-canary-1`
Lucas: perf + kv stats: `./bin/profiler --target=orchid-canary-1 --workload=longseq && ./bin/kvstats --pool=orchid-canary-1`
Mike: rollback criteria (pre-agreed): if p95 increases >12% for 20m OR kv_miss_rate > 0.08 OR any GPU stalls >= 200ms across >30% of requests -> immediate rollback to flashv2 and pause rollout.
Priya: timeline proposal: start tomorrow 09:00 UTC, run 5% for 6h, if stable expand to 25% for 12h, then 100% after another 24h. Run prompt-suite after each stage.
Owen: ownership: @Lucas prototype selector + unit tests, @Jessica run canary + orchestrate rollouts, @Priya run eval suite and compare outputs, @Mike own alerts and rollback automation.
Jessica: adding a couple technical knobs to test in canary: `kv.page_size` tweak, `batcher.max_coalesce_ns`, and `kernel.chunk_size_hint`. Suggested test matrix: page_size {1MB,2MB,4MB}, coalesce {5ms,20ms}, chunk_hint {64,128,256}.
Lucas: note: try `kv.page_size=2MB` — reduced TLB pressure in previous workloads. Also test with continuous-batching off to confirm effect.
Mike: will wire alerting + a Slack incident channel synched to the canary dashboard for live ops.
Priya: I'll prepare the regression prompt-suite and baseline metrics to compare (perplexity proxies + hallucination heuristics).
Jessica: I'll draft a short runbook and post it to #incidents if any metric trips. Also will add a short note to the release changelog about selector behavior. :thumbsup:
Owen: thanks — let's keep the communication tight during the first 12h.
Lucas: one more thought — if we see persistent kv-miss spikes, consider a hybrid: FA3 for short seqs & fused-attn for long paged sequences (different memory access pattern).
Jessica: adding hybrid rule to the fflag if experiments point there. Thanks everyone, will post a status update in ~2h once initial canary is up.
